newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian civil servants to strike over govt cuts.
newsitem.headline: Australian civil servants to strike over govt cuts.

text.p: Thousands of Australian civil servants will begin a series of strikes around the country from May 2 to protest against government cutbacks, a leading union leader said on Wednesday.
Commonwealth Public Sector Union national secretary Wendy Caird said union members, angry at job losses and changes to employment conditions, voted overwhelmingly at nation-wide meetings to strike.
"From May 2 we'll have two hour strikes in the afternoon and they'll be on a state-by-state basis," Caird told Reuters.
"So every day from May 2 until the end of the following week there will be some stoppage action around Australia."

Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith played down the likely impact of the strikes, saying negotiations had not broken down. "The rank and file trade union members that I've been speaking to have not been supporting the (union) ... and are prepared to sit down and talk to us in a sensible way," he said.

Caird said the year-old conservative government was expected to axe more jobs in the budget for 1997/98 to June 30, due to be announced on May 13, after slashing thousands of jobs in the previous budget and a series of other reforms.
The government would not provide any money for civil servant pay rises over the next two years, Caird said.
Union members would consider further action in a series of meetings from May 12 if the government failed to act, she said.
The union represents 60,000 of Australia's 130,000 federal public servants.
